title: Today / Morning Brief
markdown:
`openexecutive.api.routes.today` serves the morning brief — a one-screen, read-only view of what is happening across the org. It is the default landing surface (the Next.js root renders `<Briefing>`).

`GET /today` returns `TodayResponse` assembled by `_build_today()`, which is synchronous and caller-agnostic:

- **`departments`** — per-department goal health, rolling up each department's goal counts (`total`, `at_risk`, `off_track`) plus its awaiting-workflow count, and `attention_goals`: the actual off-track/at-risk goals (worst first, capped at 3) with `key_result`, `current`, `target`, and `status`, so the briefing's Department card shows *which* goal is off and how far without a click. Empty for healthy/inactive departments.
- **`people`** — an attention-ranked roster. Each person carries `awaiting_action` count, soonest SLA, a `status` (`on_leave` / `needs_reply` / `awaiting` / `clear`), reachability, `overdue`, a server `priority` sort key, and a cached one-line `insight`. Sorted by `(-priority, full_name)`.
- **`proposals`** — the *live* unread alerts (workflow approvals, triage-classified inbound, Executive signals, flagged artifacts, and gated calendar bookings): unread, inside their category TTL, not snoozed — see *Alert lifecycle* below. Each carries `score`, `category` (`action` vs `monitoring`), `surfaced_reason` from `openexecutive.briefing.ranking`, the lifecycle fields (`occurrence_count`, `last_seen_at`, `last_reviewed_at`, `review_verdict`, `review_note`, `recommended_move`, `why_now`, `due_at`, `superseded_count`, `suggested_workflow`), and `decision_instance_id` (set only when the proposal is backed by a decision-ledger row — a calendar booking awaiting approval). The UI splits them into 'mine' vs 'across the team' using `caller_person_id`. For decision-backed proposals the card's Approve/Reject call the `/decisions` endpoints (which book or cancel the event server-side and clear the alert) instead of the ack-and-hand-off-to-chat flow — so meeting bookings are reviewed in the briefing itself rather than on a separate page.
- **`narrative`** — a per-viewer Executive-voice header synthesized by `synthesize_briefing_narrative`; the principal gets the whole-company scope, teammates a role-scoped one. In the web UI each bullet of this narrative is a click target: clicking one hands off to chat (the same `onContinue` path as the proposal cards) seeded to discuss that item. The Executive recognizes it because every chat turn now carries a `<briefing>` digest of open alerts (see Memory).
- **`in_flight`** / **`awaiting`** — upcoming Executive commitments and people we are waiting on.
- **`handled_overnight`** — the autonomous moves the Executive *completed* since the last delivered morning brief: the alert review's (routed, nudged, escalated, drafted, merged, closed) plus the research watch policy's (`watching` — a watch added on its own because it was grounded in company data; `stopped_watching` — a research watch auto-disabled as noisy or dead; no alert id, re-enable from `/watchlist`). A `changed` verdict (the review rewrote an open alert's headline / body / severity) is deliberately **not** here: the alert is still open in "Needs you" and its card carries the note, so the brief reports it under "what changed" (a REWRITTEN block) rather than as done. Each row is structured, not just a sentence: `kind`, the audit `summary` (nudge bookkeeping marker stripped), `at`, `alert_id`, `event_type` (for a pre-filtered `/audit` deep link), `headline` (the alert's headline at move time; a watch's slug), `target` (person name for routed / nudged, survivor headline for merged, new severity for escalated, draft title, workflow name), `detail` (the cited evidence or the watch policy's reason), `outcome` (`resolved` | `dismissed` for a close, `proposed` for a route that went through the authority gate), `evidence_ref` (S1 / R2 / A3), `superseded_by_alert_id`, and `status` — the alert's lifecycle state **now** (`open` = live in the queue per `lifecycle.is_live` | `resolved` | `dismissed` | `expired` | `merged` | `acked` | `inactive` for snoozed / past-TTL rows), looked up per row so a close the principal already undid renders as reopened instead of offering a second Undo, and a "still open" jump link only appears when there is a card to land on. The morning brief also carries a one-line count of research watch suggestions waiting on `/watchlist`.

The route resolves the caller from `x-caller-email`, then attaches the viewer-scoped narrative in a `BackgroundTask` so the request never blocks on an LLM call. `GET /today/activity` returns the recent self-initiated action rail — merged from fired scheduled actions (DMs, follow-ups, nudges, cadences), logged decisions, saved advice, completed workflow runs (briefings/check-ins/research), kicked-off initiatives, resolved gated decisions, and raised alerts, so it reflects all of the Executive's activity rather than just dispatched messages. The Pulse page (`/memories`) polls it (limit 100) every ~20s so new events stream into the 'Recent activity' card, which scrolls internally at a fixed height instead of growing the page. The `morning_brief` workflow calls `_build_today()` directly to build the standalone DM (via a different, enumerated prompt). `GET /morning-brief` is a deprecated alias.

## Alert lifecycle & the Executive review

Alerts used to be write-once: raised, then never looked at again, so the "Needs you" queue grew without bound and the briefs re-listed it daily. Three things now keep it live:

- **Time-to-live** (`openexecutive.alerts.lifecycle`). Action items expire after `ALERT_TTL_DAYS_ACTION` (14 d), unrouted low/medium monitoring signals after `ALERT_TTL_DAYS_MONITORING` (3 d). Every surface reads `list_live_alerts` (the same predicate the scheduler's 15-minute sweep persists as status `expired`), so `/today` is right even before the sweep runs. Artifacts and decision-backed alerts are exempt. `POST /alerts/{id}/reopen` is the Undo.
- **Coalescing** (`alerts.pipeline` + `store.coalesce_alert`). A repeat of an open alert with the same `(source, dedup_key)` updates that row — `occurrence_count`, `last_seen_at`, severity max — instead of stacking a second card, and only re-pings when severity rose to high/urgent. Monitoring alerts carry a stable `watch:<slug>` key, so one watch means one card.
- **The review** (`openexecutive.alerts.review`, heartbeat `alert_review_scan`, every 6 h and right before the morning brief). For each open alert the Executive sees what changed since it was raised — newer signals from the same watch, related alerts, activity since, the roster with SLAs, department authority — and returns a verdict (relevant / changed / resolved / stale) plus a recommended move. Deterministic policy then acts: **route** (assign + DM the owner; `propose_via_alert` for propose-only departments), **nudge**, **escalate** (severity + `due_at` + DM the principal only), **draft** (`draft_artifact`), **suggest a workflow** (a link, never a run), **merge** (`superseded_by_alert_id`), or **resolve** — only on high confidence citing a server-minted evidence ref (a newer signal, a related alert, an activity item shown for that alert); free text never closes a card, and anything weaker is annotated `likely_stale`, demoted 30 ranking points, and left for one click. Everything that came from outside is rendered as inert data inside the review prompt, so an injected email body cannot steer the batch. Board / comp / legal matters only ever go to a scope-holder or the principal and keep their text. Route and escalate are idempotent across passes, every DM carries an "[Alert review] Re: …" header, outbound moves are capped per pass, passes are single-flight, `ALERT_REVIEW_ENABLED=false` stops every caller, every move is audited with its evidence and prior state, and a distinct `resolved` status keeps Executive closes separate from `ack` (user approved).

On the page, cards read as decisions: the one-line "what changed since you last looked" (`review_note`) leads, the recommended move is the primary control (Nudge <owner> → chat; Run <workflow> → `/jobs/<name>`), with chips for age, seen ×N, why-now / due, folded-in and draft-ready, a "Reviewed <ago>" footer, and an amber Likely-stale treatment with one-click Dismiss. "Needs you" shows *Start here* + 8 cards + "Show N more", a "Dismiss N older than 7 days" footer (explicit ids to `POST /alerts/bulk-ack` — never a server-side age sweep, which would hit teammates' routed items), and "Re-check relevance" (`POST /alerts/review`). The handled rail (anchor of the "Executive handled N overnight" pill) is deliberately one sentence by default: a first-person heading built from counts only — "Since your last brief: N off your plate (closes still standing, and merges whose survivor is not itself listed; a merge into a listed survivor counts on that survivor's row), N in others' hands (routed / nudged), N waiting on you (escalated)", plus "N drafts ready", "N workflows suggested", "N watch changes", "N other moves" (a kind the UI does not know) and "N back on your plate" (a close that is open again) when present — with the rows behind a "details" disclosure, and nothing rendered at all when the grouped rows are empty. The pure logic (grouping, headline, links) lives in `packages/ui/src/lib/handled.ts` and is covered by `npm test`. Expanded, it shows one first-person row per alert ("Resolved *X* — evidence", "Dismissed *X* as stale — evidence", "Handed *X* to Dana Kim" / "Proposed *X* to Dana Kim (awaiting their approval)", "Chased Dana Kim on *X*", "Raised *X* to high", "Drafted *T* from *X*", "Folded *X* into *Y*", "Started watching *slug*"), escalations first; rows sharing an alert collapse to the newest move with the others as an "also …" trailer — a close always keeps the visible slot (it carries Undo), otherwise an escalation beats routed / nudged / drafted; a merge whose survivor is listed becomes "N duplicates folded in" on the survivor. Every row links its `evidence_ref` (or "evidence") to `/audit?event_type=…&q=…` (the audit page pre-fills those filters from the query string), a still-open row jumps to its card (`#alert-<id>`), drafted rows link `/artifacts`, watch rows `/watchlist`. Undo is offered only while the close still stands (`status` not `open`); a reverted close shows "Reopened". Dismissing a watch-sourced alert lowers that watch's `trust_score` (which discounts ranking and is shown to the review as evidence); the ack body may carry `mute_topic`.

## Multi-client practice section

In multi-client practice mode (2+ client slots — see the Client Companies section), the response gains an additive `practice_clients` list: rollup cards for the **parked** clients (overdue follow-ups, awaiting replies, unread alerts, onboarding due soon, renewal countdowns), each stamped with the save point its data reflects. Single-company installs always receive an empty list and the UI renders nothing.
